edges.demand: A convex body of affine dimension k holds at most k!·vol + k lattice points.
A gradient of an arithmetic circuit takes constant work per circuit operation.
A basis of a saturated lattice extends to an ambient unimodular basis. Minkowski’s second theorem and Mahler’s basis bound give the basis norm product bounds h, 2h and 9h at ranks one, two and three.
The Moore determinant on F_q-independent entries is nonzero.
A symmetric convex body of volume 2^d·det contains a nonzero lattice point: the short multiple.
The symbolic game and real run agree until two values collide by lazy sampling of the label maps.
A nonzero polynomial of degree ≤d_f vanishes on the valid coin grid with probability at most d_f/(q−D).
The factor ϖ clears target differences from χκ and source differences to polynomials in the coins and r of total degree ≤d_f.
For 2β<q and 24β⁴<q³, lifting is correct for nonzero v with v_0=0 and takes poly(N,log q).
Under (I1)–(I6), a nonzero vector v with v_0=0 and gp(vᵀ)>θ admits a short multiple.

add.label: Direct inverse
add.name: Inverse theorem
add.statement: Under (I1)–(I6), every nonzero v∈F_q^{N+1} with v_0=0 and gp(vᵀ)>θ has a short multiple x with x_0=0.
add.proof:
Write ε=ε_tr and μ=μ_tr. On the independent uniform box {2,…,g+1}, a rank-e fiber has mass ≤g^{−e}: fixing the coordinates outside an invertible basis minor fixes the rest.

Trimming. For a lattice Θ of rank 1≤d≤3 with basis B, a centered box coordinate has moment generating function sinh(gt/2)/(g sinh(t/2)) by a geometric sum, with limit 1 at zero. Since sinh(x)/x≥1 and (2j+1)!≥6^jj!, this is at most exp(g²t²/24). Thus the centered image Y=Bᵀr_I−y_Θ satisfies E e^{uᵀY}≤e^{uᵀΣ_Θu/2} by independence. For Z=Σ_Θ^{−1/2}Y and an independent standard Gaussian G in dimension d, integrate e^{√(99/100)GᵀZ} in either order: E e^{99‖Z‖²/200}≤E e^{99‖G‖²/200}=10^d. Markov's inequality and (I2) bound the mass removed by 10^d e^{−99R_tr²/200}≤ε.

Integral facts. For rows J of a largest minor, Cramer's rule makes each entry of B_iB_J^{−1} a ratio of a maximal minor to det B_J, hence at most one in magnitude. Thus restriction to J is injective on the span, and ‖y‖_∞≤‖y_J‖₁ there. For saturated Θ a unimodular extension of B gives an integral left inverse, so Bᵀ is onto the integer codomain. For rank-k Δ with k-minors of magnitude <q, a nonzero minor survives, so each nonzero Smith diagonal entry in UΔV=S is a unit mod q. If cᵀΔ≡0, the first k entries of cᵀU^{−1} are multiples of q. Set them to zero and multiply by U. This gives an integral relation reducing to cᵀ.

Prefixes. Put J first for a saturated rank-d Θ. Let B_k be the first k rows, d≤k≤|I|, and write B_k=Y_kC_k with Y_k a basis of the integer points of its span and C_k integral. These prefix lattices have rank d and largest minor J. If h_k,m_k are height and maximum fiber mass, then h_k[Z^d:B_kᵀZ^k]=h(Θ): the index is |det C_k| by transpose surjectivity, and minors scale by that determinant. The first prefix is Z^d, with h_d=1 and m_d=g^{−d}; the last is Θ. Adding a row enlarges the transpose image by a cyclic quotient of order s_k=h_{k+1}/h_k. The new coordinate must lie in one class mod s_k in a fiber, and B_kᵀ and Y_kᵀ have the same fibers by invertibility of C_k. Thus m_{k+1}≤m_k⌈g/s_k⌉/g≤m_k, and s_k≥g fixes the new coordinate.
For s=s_k<g we have m_{k+1}^b h_{k+1}^{b−1}≤m_k^b h_k^{b−1}. For s=1 this is monotonicity. Otherwise ⌈g/s⌉/g≤(1+s/g)/s≤s^{−1+1/b}. The last inequality holds for s≥2^b since 1+s/g≤2, and for 2≤s≤2^b by concavity of s^{1/b}−1−s/2^b and g≥2^b. The concave function is zero at 2^b and positive at 2 by ln(2)/b>2^{1−b} for b≥7 (true at 7, with b/2^{b−1} decreasing).
For rank three, the r ratios above one multiply to h=h(Θ). The upper density factor ∏(1/s_k+1/g) over these ratios exceeds 1/h by at most r(1/2+1/g)^{r−1}/g, by telescoping one factor at a time. If r=0 this error is zero; otherwise the bound is maximal at r=2, since the successive ratio after that is (1+1/r)(1/2+1/g)<1. Therefore m(Θ)≤g^{−3}ξ_tr(1/h+1/g). If m(Θ)≥μ, solving for h gives h≤H_3 by (I2); then m(Θ)h≤Γ_3/g³ by (I4).

Image count. Let rank-d Θ on |I|≤N trim nonempty F on I and i′, with d∈{1,2,3}. An image point of Φ(r)=(Bᵀr_I,r_{i′}) has mass ≤m(Θ)/g. For a full-dimensional image in an index-q coset project identically with k=d+1, δ=q, B_2=B, J=∅ and A=1.
Otherwise suppose F^⊥ has rank 1≤d′<d, largest minor J⊆I, with restrictions to I in span B. Then B_J contains the column span of Y_J for a normal basis Y, so has rank d′. Extend its integral kernel basis to a unimodular basis of Z^d, putting the kernel last. The changed B=(B_1,B_2) has (B_2)_J=0 and (B_1)_J invertible, and defines Φ without changing trimming. Its transpose (a,t)↦(Ba,t) identifies real normal spaces of Φ(F) and F by the restriction hypothesis. Thus k=dim Φ(F)=d+1−d′. Split the saturated image normal basis V into first d′ rows V_1 and the rest V_2. Pullback gives (B_1)_JV_1=Y_JC with C integral nonsingular, so Aδ≥h(F^⊥) for A=|det(B_1)_J| and δ=|det V_1|. Drop the first d′ coordinates, injectively on ker Vᵀ. The remaining differences satisfy V_2ᵀx≡0 mod V_1ᵀZ^{d′}, a subgroup of index δ by transpose surjectivity.
The projected hull is k-dimensional in an index-δ coset. A lattice simplex has edge determinant a nonzero multiple of δ, so vol≥δ/k!, so the lattice point bound is k!·vol/δ+k≤(k+1)!·vol/δ. The hull fits an interval of length ≤g times the projected ellipsoid of dimension j=k−1. Its volume is vol(Ball_j)(gR_tr/√12)^j√det(B_2ᵀB_2) by singular values, where Ball_j is the Euclidean unit ball. By Cauchy–Binet, A√det(B_2ᵀB_2)≤h(Θ)√binom(N,j), since (B_2)_J=0 makes each product minor a maximal minor of B. Using binom(N,j)≤N^j/j!,
Pr[F]·Aδ≤m(Θ)h(Θ)g^j R_tr^j N^{j/2}(j+2)!vol(Ball_j)/√(12^j j!).
For j=1,2,3 the last factor is 2√3, √2π or 20π/(9√2), respectively. By (I3) this gives Pr[F]≤Λ_d g^d h(Θ)m(Θ)/q, and otherwise Pr[F]h(F^⊥)≤Λ_{d−d′}g^{d−d′}h(Θ)m(Θ).

Regularization. For saturated Θ on ≤N indices of rank d∈{1,2,3} with m≥μ+(3−d)ε, find a saturated regular extension of rank ≤3 losing ≤(3−d)ε. Descend from d=3 by the prefix bound. For d≤2 choose each prefix's largest fiber and trim by R_{k−1} if present, yielding F_k with mass ≥m_k−ε≥μ+(2−d)ε. If F_k^⊥ strictly contains Θ_k, its rank e exceeds d by saturation and is ≤3 since Pr[F_k]>g^{−4}. Its density meets μ+(3−e)ε. Induction gives a regular extension R_k with mass ≥m_k−(3−d)ε. If present at the last prefix, use it.
Otherwise let j be the last index with R_j, or d−1. For k≥j+1, F_{k+1}^⊥=Θ_{k+1}; s_k≥g would put its new unit normal in Θ_{k+1}, vanishing on J, contrary to injectivity. Thus m_k(m_kh_k)^{b−1} decreases from j+1, and the final m≥μ makes regularity follow if the product at j+1 is ≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1}. For j=d−1 this is g^{−db}≤μ(Γ_d/g^d)^{b−1}. Otherwise F_{j+1} is trimmed by R_j of rank e>d and its normals form Θ_{j+1}, with largest minor J and restrictions in span(Θ_j)⊆span(R_j). The second image count and regularity give Pr[F_{j+1}]h_{j+1}≤Λ_{e−d}Γ_e/g^d. By (I4), m_{j+1}≤A_inv Pr[F_{j+1}] and m_{j+1}≤m_j≤Pr[F_j]+ε≤g^{−d−1}+ε≤μP_d^{b−1}. Multiplying the bounds gives the desired product using A_invΛ_{e−d}Γ_eP_d≤Γ_d.

Support induction. Relabel to put the m nonzero positive coordinates first. Conditioning on added independent summands shows that each nonempty prefix has guessing probability ≥gp(vᵀ)>θ; conditioning on all but one nonzero coordinate bounds it by 1/g. Maintain a regular saturated Θ of rank d≤3 whose reduction contains v_{[i]} and with density at least gp(v_{[i]}ᵀ)−3ε>μ. For i=1 use Z, onto modulo q, with h=1 and m(Θ)=1/g. This is regular since (I4) and μ<1/g give Γ_1≥1. For all prefixes h≤H_d by regularity (d≤2) or the rank-three bound.
On the largest-minor projection of determinant h, the ℓ₁ ball volume 2^d/d! gives minima product ≤d!h by Minkowski II. Mahler gives basis lengths ≤λ₁,λ₂,3λ₃/2 as present. Lifting via the coordinate bound gives ∏‖B_j‖_∞≤a_d h with a_d=1,2,9 respectively. Set v_{[i]}≡Bc′, c=(c′,v_{i+1}) and trim a largest modular fiber cᵀΦ=t. The result F has density ≥gp(v_{[i+1]}ᵀ)−ε>μ. Its image lies in an index-q coset because v_{i+1}≠0. Full dimension would force Pr[F]≤Λ_dΓ_d/q<μ by the image bound and (I5).
For the difference matrix Δ of the image, rank k≤d, the j-th moment row has entries bounded by 2R_tr√[(Σ_Θ)_{jj}]≤T_tr‖B_j‖_∞ by Cauchy–Schwarz. The new-coordinate row is bounded by g−1≤T_tr. Each bound is at least one if we use T_tr for the last row. Thus the k-minors are bounded by d!T_tr^d∏‖B_j‖_∞≤d!a_d H_dT_tr^d<q by (I5). Since cᵀΔ≡0, lift c integrally and pull it back by Φᵀ to a member of F^⊥ reducing to v_{[i+1]}. This normal lattice has positive rank, at most three by the fiber bound, and m(F^⊥)≥Pr[F]>θ−ε≥μ+2ε. Its regular extension loses ≤2ε, giving the next prefix.
At i=m take Bz_0≡v_{[m]}≠0. The inverse image of the line of z_0 modulo q has index q^{d−1}, and its dominant-minor projection has determinant h q^{d−1}. By (I6) and integrality of h, d!h q^{d−1}≤β^d. The ℓ₁ ball of radius β reaches Minkowski's volume threshold, so shrinking to equality if needed gives a nonzero projected point B_Jz. Lift back to 0<‖Bz‖_∞≤‖B_Jz‖₁≤β<q. Thus its residue is a nonzero multiple of the prefix, and zero padding and inverse relabeling give the result with x_0=0.

add.label: Direct view
add.name: View
add.statement: Every extractor output is ⊥ or a witness. In admissible extraction put u=2Q+2. The init and charged first-mark probabilities are bounded respectively by ε_fΣ_s binom(L_s,2) and N_cmp(u)(θ+ε_f)+(binom(L+3u,2)+L+3u)ε_f. A target run has a first mark in {init, guess, charged, good}. A guess first mark has probability ≤2^λ/N_free for Q_H≤2^λ. For bit b let s_b be B_b's success on uniform Module-SIS. A good first mark with a kernel vector in its row space has probability ≤s_b+2ε_f. A good first mark with no kernel vector there and no witness output has probability ≤2/q. Witness moment polynomials satisfy both division identities with allowed remainder and quotients of degree <D. Under (P5), E(u)≤(Q+1)/2^λ for integers 0≤Q<2^λ. For adversary time t and ≤Q_H queries per RO, both reductions take at most t+O(Q+d_RQ_H+μ)+poly(D,log q) in the prescribed model. For uniform b, Pr[b′=b and Fail]≤1/2+(f_0+f_1)/4.
add.proof:
Quotient criterion for symmetric W. For R_W=Σ_k r_kX^k the coset δ_t G has sum νΣ_j r_{νj}(δ_t^ν)^j by summing monomials. The Vandermonde on distinct δ_t^ν makes vanishing of all sums equivalent to allowedness, including the empty case R_W=0. By the table these are the constraint tests. The difference P_W−Z_0R_W vanishes on cosets and d_0, with values at d_j equal to Booleanity tests. Divisibility by Z is exactly their vanishing. At ρ the difference is W_{00}, so subtract W_{00}L_ρ for key division. Evaluation on the cosets forces R=R_W since Z_0 is nonzero there. Numerator degrees ≤2D−2 and divisor degrees D−1,D yield quotients below D. The witness moment matrix passes and has corner one, giving both divisions.

At fixed r, clearing denominators of val(D)−χκ gives degree ≤d_f for any target expression D and χ∈F_q. Valid coins form a product grid of factor sizes ≥q−D, with no zero denominator. By (P5), 24ε_f≤E(2)≤2^{−λ}, so ε_f=(d_f+61)/(q−D)<1 and q−D>d_f. Schwartz–Zippel gives the coincidence bound and makes an identity on this grid a rational function identity.
At an identity fix r. Write a=Ω_{12}, b=Ω_{22}. Only H has poles in b. Multiply by b, set b=0 and cancel the remaining denominator factors, which do not involve a,b. For each index j, substitute y=B(τ)+t e_j and read degree one in t. Only the j-th H pole contributes, since its two pole numerators before substitution are −aα_s s_leg(B_j−y_j) and α_s s_leg(B_j−y_j). Thus Σ_{s,leg}α_s s_leg(L_2−aL_1)=0, with L_m the sum of first-group exponents against the corresponding H_m weighted by the expression coefficients D_{U,V} for first input U and second input V, evaluated at b=0,y=B(τ).
In these sums, the only a-dependent first-group exponents are the second F coordinates, aπ_{k_1}B_i(τ). The other types are 1, ζτ^k, ζ′τ^k, ζ″B_i(τ) and π_{k_1}B_i(τ). After multiplying by α_s s_leg they separate by α sector and by the displayed scalar factors. Without π, s_X υ^{k_leg} distinguishes legs. With π, its ε-degree-zero factor is π s_X υ^{k_c}, distinguishing cells by kind and exponent. Within each type the powers of τ, or the B_i, are independent, the latter by B(d_i)=e_i. Thus degree two in a forces every F_2 coefficient against H_1 to vanish. Degree one kills all remaining H_1 coefficients except F_1 and matches each F_1,H_1 coefficient with its F_2,H_2 coefficient.
Now select the sector and homogeneous class π in the exponents. The compatible pairs are the matched F,H coordinates, F_1 with search bases or G_2, and quotient, remainder and cancellation powers with their respective bases. In the matched pair the two hidden-basis matrices cancel. After division by α_s, the factor table gives Σ_c γ_c b_c+Φ=χ_sκ with χ_plain=χ and χ_α=−D_K, where
b_c=yᵀ(W_c r−u_c)+yᵀ(W_c−W_cᵀ)A(τ)+(P_{W_c}+h_c Z_c+Z_0 R_c)(τ).
The powers give h_c and an allowed R_c. Each b_c is free of ε,υ,s_X; Φ contains only masks, G_2 pairs and cancellation pairs and is free of s_X. The ε-degree-zero s_X υ^{k_c} coefficients give b_key=χ_s L_ρ and all other b_c=0, and Φ=0. The same separation, with y_i, identifies each row. The y-linear part at d_0 gives W_c r=u_c; at ρ and d_j it kills every column of W_c−W_cᵀ. The y-constant part gives the quotient criterion with an allowed remainder (negate h_c,R_c), with key corner χ_s by evaluation at ρ. Thus the matrices pass. In Φ the ε-degree-zero η_a coefficient is π yᵀt_a(υ) plus a multiple of πP(υ) from the tie bases. Cancel π and take each y_i coefficient to obtain the ties.
Only H_1 contains r, through α_s s_leg r_j, and it pairs only with F_1 as proved above. Therefore changing r by Δr changes the sector by α_s Σ_c γ_c yᵀW_c Δr. A zero stack in each sector extends the identity to every r and gives χ=0 by the key corner. Conversely, formal identity forces W_c r=u_c for all r, so the stacks vanish. Applied to a difference this gives stack equality under formal equality. A source-group difference paired with the opposite generator is a target expression with zero stacks and the same value. If not formally zero it cannot be identically zero at any fixed r, so the target coincidence bound applies.

First-mark bounds. For init, injectivity means that a formally distinct received pair shares its label only if its exponents coincide. Apply the fixed-r bounds just proved, sum over the same-group pairs and average over r.
The coupled uniform-mask and symbolic transcripts agree until a collision, including a guess equal to an assigned exponent. A charged mark cannot start at an initial collision. A good first collision before a target query would be a difference mark: the later entry is a result, since a fresh guess cannot cancel in the difference, and the result meets the old label. If the target query precedes any collision, a missing entry makes a guess mark and a good target-value entry gives a good key mark. A charged first mark therefore requires a bad symbolic event. M4 ensures target coverage.
Fix the independent symbolic transcript. If the difference depends on guesses, some nonconstant guess monomial has a formally nonzero coefficient. It is a field scalar or source expression and stays nonzero as a function of the coins for each r by the coincidence bound for source groups. The clearing factor ϖ=Ω_{22}ζζ′ζ″ε has degree five. A guess times a source expression has cleared degree at most d_f+1 by the degree bound; a product of two guesses has cleared degree at most 7, and a single guess at most 6. Thus the nonzero comparison polynomial has degree at most d_f+1. The evaluation grid includes independent uniform guesses, so the zero probability is ≤(d_f+1)/(q−D)≤ε_f. Without guesses, source coincidences and nonidentity target equalities cost ≤ε_f. An identity for a bad target comparison lies in the selected stack's fiber, and the stack is nonzero since zero implies formal equality and χ=0. It must be light by badness, so such r have total probability ≤θ. This gives θ+ε_f.
At most three entries per call give at most binom(L+3u,2) pairs and L+3u target-value comparisons with guesses. Without guesses, a first collision pairs the result at call j with one of at most L+3j−1 entries; a target value can be one of two received target entries or at most Q results. This gives QL+3Q(Q+1)/2+2≤N_cmp(u) at u=2Q+2. Sum the bounds.

Rank and reduction. Stack the rows as M and take a column basis including 0 if nonzero, ignoring a zero column 0. Fix nonpivot positive coordinates. A fiber fixes the pivot residues, each positive pivot costing an independent factor ≤1/g. For a zero-index pivot condition last on all positive coordinates, costing another factor ≤1/g. Thus a rank-d fiber has mass ≤g^{−d}, and g^{−d}≥gp(W)>θ>g^{−4} for a heavy stack by (P3). For a row-space vector, vᵀr is a linear image of Mr, so a largest fiber maps to one scalar value and gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W).

 Programming the seed entries with the independent uniform challenge blocks gives the real experiment law, since all other entries and injections retain their original laws. The private draws are independent and change no simulated reply, so drawing them early preserves the output law.
Fix a good first mark with expression D and stack W. The record invariant gives D up to formal equality from the target record for a key mark, or from the marked result minus the old record for a difference. Earlier target result matches were formally equal or they would have set a mark. Thus the difference is the first private disagreement if its cleared polynomial does not vanish. It is nonzero by formal distinction and the nonvanishing denominator. Its degree is ≤d_f, so the independent test point misses with probability ≤d_f/(q−D)≤ε_f.
Any formal representative remains an identity at the run's r and has the same stacks. The hidden-basis restriction permits only F_1 paired with the r-dependent H_1 terms. Thus each gradient in sector s is α_sΣ_{c,i} γ_c y_i W^s_{c,i}, with W^s_{c,i} row i of the sector cell. An alpha mark has zero plain gradient. If a functional φ on the mark row space is nonzero, applying it to the gradient and dividing by α_sπ gives a degree-≤n+2 polynomial: γ_c/π=s_X υ^{k_c}(1+εω^{2k_1}), and the distinct monomials s_X υ^{k_c}y_i include a nonzero row coefficient. Conditioned on earlier gradients with proper span, choose such φ annihilating that span. Schwartz–Zippel bounds the chance the next gradient stays in it by (n+2)/(q−D). Since the mark rank is ≤3, three probes span except with probability at most 3(n+2)/(q−D)≤ε_f, using n≤D.
If the mark space has a kernel vector, successful detection and spanning give the lift a kernel input from that space, by the sector order. For this v, z(v)=0 gives v_0=0, and gp(vᵀ)≥gp(W)>θ, so the inverse bound under (P3) and lifting under (P3),(P4) yield a short multiple. Any returned lift from any kernel vector has x_0≡0 mod q and |x_0|≤β<q, hence x_0=0. Its remaining coefficients and zero padding give a nonzero packed vector of norm ≤β, killed modulo q by the challenge via the forms identity. Any earlier success is also a solution. Integrating the two failure bounds over the experiment, the good kernel mark probability is at most s_b+2ε_f.

The u² coefficient of E is θ/2+5ε_f≥0. By (P5), at 2 and 2^{λ+1} the function lies below u/2^{λ+1}. Convexity gives the same throughout the interval. Set u=2Q+2.

First prove witness existence for a nonzero usable rank-≤3 stack with no kernel vector. Let U have a base-field basis of its row space as columns, and u_j be its transposed rows. Write K=F_{q^n}, d=rank U, and h_s=Uᵀσ^s(z). The entries of h_0 are F_q-independent because z has no kernel there. Put a=n/2−1,b=n/2,c=n/2+1. The entries of h_a stay F_q-independent. Their nonzero Moore determinant makes the first d consecutive conjugates independent, so h_a,h_b,h_c span K^d.
The three assemblies W_s are the U-weight matrix, V-weight matrix and σ^c of the U-weight matrix, respectively. Each is UM_sUᵀ with unique symmetric M_s, by applying a left inverse of U on both sides since the rows and columns lie in its span. The ties give M_s h_t=M_t h_s. A relation on the h_s therefore gives the same relation on the M_s by testing on spanning vectors. Extend h_s↦M_s linearly to M(h). The trilinear form T(h,u,v)=uᵀM(h)v is symmetric by the ties and matrix symmetry. Booleanity on each assembly and the spanning of the h_s give T(h,u_j,u_j−u_0)=0. Since σ^{a+c} is the identity and the V assembly is even in T, M_a=σ^a(M_c) and M_b=σ^b(M_b).
If u_0=0, choose a basis from the other rows. T vanishes on repeated basis arguments, so only d=3 can leave a nonzero value t on distinct arguments. In this basis the off-diagonal entries of M_s are t times the corresponding complementary coordinates of h_s. Conjugacy then gives t h_a=σ^a(t)h_0 and t h_b=σ^b(t)h_0. If t≠0, h_a and h_b are multiples of h_0, so the three h_s cannot span dimension three. Thus T vanishes, contrary to the nonzero stack.
Otherwise complete u_0 to a basis l_0=u_0,l_1,…,l_{d−1} of rows. Let p_δ be the vector with pairings (1,δ) against this basis for a binary tuple δ. Put w_δ=Up_δ and z_δ=z(w_δ)≠0. Symmetry and Booleanity reduce each basis triple to its subset A of nonzero indices, replacing repetitions by zero indices. The cubes (hᵀp_δ)(uᵀp_δ)(vᵀp_δ) evaluate there as 1_{A⊆supp δ}. This matrix is triangular with unit diagonal in cardinality order, so the cubes span T. Pairs also realize all subsets since d−1≤2, making the squares p_δp_δᵀ independent. Thus M_s=Σ_δ c_δ σ^s(z_δ)p_δp_δᵀ. Comparing square coefficients in the two conjugacy identities fixes c_δ/z_δ under σ^a and σ^b, hence under σ. Put χ_δ=c_δ/z_δ∈F_q.
Any base-field passage test L vanishes on W_s by linearity from the passing cells and by conjugation for W_c. Thus it gives h_0ᵀQh_s=0 with Q=Σ_δ χ_δ L(w_δw_δᵀ)p_δp_δᵀ over F_q. Spanning gives h_0ᵀQ=0 and F_q-independence gives Q=0. Thus independent squares force χ_δ L(w_δw_δᵀ)=0. Some χ_δ≠0 since the stack is nonzero. Its w_δ has corner one and passes all tests, so is a witness.

The tests return only checked witnesses. For a good difference mark the record invariant gives its expression in the tested difference. For a good key mark the target record gives its expression. It comes from a tested result, since input target elements have zero stacks and fresh guesses carry a guess variable. Formal equality preserves stacks and thus sketches. Therefore the mark-sector sketches are tested unless a witness is already returned.
For its symmetric stack W, the probe map (v_c)_c↦Σ_c W_c v_c surjects onto the row space V, since symmetry identifies the column spans with row spans. The three sketches are independent uniform points of V, independently of the run through the mark. The heavy rank bound gives d=dim V≤3. Then their coordinate matrix in a basis has d independent uniform rows in F_q³. The chance of rank loss is at most Σ_{j=0}^{d−1}q^{j−3}<2/q by testing each row against the span of its predecessors. At full rank the tested span is V. The preceding argument provides a witness in V. For rank at most three a witness has coordinate 0 equal to 1, making 0 a pivot, and all its other pivot values are Boolean, so it is among the enumerated candidates. Thus the test returns a witness, and the conditional failure bound gives the claimed probability.

Reduction time. With private points sampled first, maintain in each group the assigned label-exponent bijection and the table of decided strings, including rejections. A uniform injection completion gives membership probability V/U for V unassigned exponents and U undecided strings. Accept iff a uniform draw from the explicit integer interval [1,U] is ≤V; then choose a uniform field element outside the exponent keys. An unassigned computed exponent gets a uniform string outside the decided keys. Maps and counters update in constant time and U fits the integer range since the generator is assigned. Each call handles at most two operands and one result or name negation.
